article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Strawberry Torte × Blueberry Fritter
Breeder: Square One Genetics
THC Content: 25-27%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Strawberry, blueberry, mixed berries, nuts
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–65 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Heavy
Outdoor Yield: Heavy
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Strawburst is built around fruit without becoming a simple fruit-candy strain. The first aroma can resemble fresh strawberries and crushed blueberries, but underneath that sweetness sits a distinctly richer mixture of nuts, pastry-like dough, earth, and occasional gas. That combination comes directly from a pedigree designed around two very different expressions of dessert cannabis . Strawberry Torte contributes red-berry sweetness, nutty depth, and Purple Punch influence, while Blueberry Fritter adds old-school blueberry character wrapped around Apple Fritter ‘s denser, funkier foundation. The result is weed that can smell like berry filling inside a baked dessert rather than artificial candy alone.

Square One Genetics released Strawburst as a feminized F1 created from Strawberry Torte and Blueberry Fritter. The breeder’s current genetic archive classifies it as a heavy-yielding cultivar with a 60–65 day flowering period and specifically summarizes its terpene character as blueberry, strawberry, and nutty. That official description is especially useful because several unrelated products have appeared under similar Strawberry Burst or Strawburst names. The cultivar covered here is the Square One Genetics version.
Genetics and Lineage

Strawberry Torte forms one half of the cross and already carries a remarkably rich dessert pedigree. Square One identifies Strawberry Torte as Peanut Butter Cookies × Purple Punch, with strawberry, gas, and nutty traits as its defining aromatic characteristics. Peanut Butter Cookies brings sweet roasted-nut, Cookie, and fuel qualities, while Purple Punch contributes berry, grape, floral sweetness, and a heavier physical character. The parent therefore offers much more than strawberry aroma alone; it gives Strawburst much of the creamy, nutty foundation that distinguishes the strain from cleaner berry cultivars.

Blueberry Fritter contributes the other side. Robin Hood Seeds lists its own Blueberry Fritter as Original Blueberry × Apple Fritter with an apple-and-blueberry aromatic profile and a 63–65 day flowering window. Original Blueberry introduces classic sweet berry genetics, while Apple Fritter supplies a denser blend of fruit, earth, pastry, and gas. Combined with Strawberry Torte, it creates a family tree saturated with fruit but supported by enough Cookies, Kush-related, and fuel-oriented ancestry to keep the finished marijuana complex.

That genetic structure also creates room for phenotype variation. One plant may lean heavily into sweet strawberry and blueberry, while another can emphasize nuts, baked dough, funk, or gas. Since Strawburst was released as an F1 rather than a highly inbred uniform line, growers hunting several seeds should expect some variation in plant structure, aroma balance, coloration, and finishing behavior even when the core berry identity remains recognizable.
Effects and Experience

The effects generally fit the idea of a balanced modern hybrid better than a simple indica-or-sativa label. Early in the experience, the mental side can feel brighter and more engaging, with a lift in mood and stronger interest in music, conversation, gaming, or low-pressure creative activity. The change is typically more rounded than sharply stimulating, making the opening phase feel comfortable rather than frantic when the dose remains moderate.

As the session progresses, physical relaxation becomes more noticeable. The shoulders and limbs can begin to feel heavier while the earlier mental activity settles into a calmer rhythm. That progression gives Strawburst potential versatility: smaller amounts may fit an afternoon or social setting, whereas heavier consumption is more likely to turn the same weed into an evening cultivar. The Purple Punch and Peanut Butter Cookies ancestry helps explain why the physical side can eventually become substantial even though the flavor profile feels bright and fruity.

Square One Genetics does not publish an official THC percentage for Strawburst, so assigning a universal potency figure would be misleading. Phenotype, light intensity, harvest timing, plant health, cure, and laboratory methodology can all change cannabinoid results. Consumers should use the certificate for their particular batch rather than assuming that every sample bearing the name has identical strength. As with other THC-rich cannabis, excessive intake can lead to dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, temporary memory impairment, or anxiety.
Medical Benefits

Strawburst has not been studied as an individual medical marijuana cultivar in controlled clinical research. Any discussion of possible therapeutic value therefore needs to distinguish the strain’s subjective effects from medically established outcomes. Its combination of mood elevation and later physical relaxation may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer hybrids for temporary relief from stress, reduced appetite, minor discomfort, or difficulty unwinding.

The gradual progression may also be useful for patients who do not want cannabis that becomes sedating immediately. Moderate intake may preserve enough mental engagement for relaxed daytime use, while larger amounts can become considerably heavier. That same dose sensitivity means patients with limited THC tolerance should approach high-potency batches carefully.

Aroma should not be confused with medical evidence either. Square One describes Strawburst in sensory terms—blueberry, strawberry, and nutty—but does not publish a standardized laboratory terpene panel for the cultivar. Compounds such as limonene, caryophyllene, myrcene, pinene, or linalool may appear in individual samples, but their exact proportions should be taken from the laboratory analysis of the specific flower rather than inferred from the strain name.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Berries dominate the first impression. Freshly opened flowers can produce a mixture of ripe strawberry, blueberry preserves, and darker mixed-berry sweetness. The scent becomes more interesting after the buds are broken apart, when roasted nuts, sweet dough, earth, and occasional fuel begin pushing through the fruit. That progression closely matches Square One’s official blueberry-strawberry-nutty description.

The two parents are particularly complementary here. Strawberry Torte contributes strawberry, gas, and nut qualities, while Blueberry Fritter supplies unmistakable blueberry sweetness along with Apple Fritter-derived pastry and funk. Instead of tasting like generic berry candy, stronger examples can resemble strawberry-and-blueberry baked goods with a nutty crust and a light fuel finish.

On the inhale, sweet fruit usually arrives first. Strawberry may be sharper and slightly tart, while blueberry tends to linger with a softer sweetness. Nutty dough, earth, and mild gas become more obvious on the exhale. A careful cure is valuable because overly rapid drying can flatten the volatile berry notes and leave the flower tasting mostly earthy or sweet.
Growing Information

Square One Genetics gives growers unusually useful breeder data for Strawburst. The cultivar flowers in approximately 60–65 days and is categorized as a heavy-yielding F1. That places the indoor schedule at roughly eight-and-a-half to a little over nine weeks, making it reasonably fast for a hybrid with substantial yield potential.

Plant structure may vary because of the diverse parentage, but growers can reasonably expect enough vigor to benefit from early canopy management. Topping or low-stress branch spreading can help distribute growth across several productive tops rather than allowing one main stem to dominate. Once flowers begin gaining weight, branch support may become useful on heavier phenotypes. Good airflow should be maintained throughout the canopy as berry-scented flowers increase in density.

Phenotype selection is one of the more interesting reasons to grow this cannabis from seed. The Strawberry Torte side can push toward strawberry, gas, and nuts, whereas Blueberry Fritter can increase blueberry, fruit, and pastry qualities. Growers searching for a keeper may want to evaluate several traits together rather than selecting only the largest plant. Intensity of berry aroma, resin coverage, branch strength, flower density, finishing speed, and resistance to late-flower stress all matter. Since Square One specifically rates Strawburst as a heavy yielder, the best individuals may combine premium aroma with meaningful production rather than forcing a choice between the two.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Strawburst?

Square One Genetics created Strawburst by crossing Strawberry Torte with Blueberry Fritter. Strawberry Torte is Peanut Butter Cookies × Purple Punch, while Robin Hood Seeds’ Blueberry Fritter is Original Blueberry × Apple Fritter.
Who bred the Strawburst strain?
Strawburst was bred by Square One Genetics. The breeder lists it in its official cultivar archive as a feminized F1 that originally appeared as a freebie release.
What does Strawburst taste like?

The breeder describes its core profile as blueberry, strawberry, and nutty. Depending on phenotype and cure, the flavor can also include sweet dough, mixed berries, earth, pastry-like richness, and light gas.
Is Strawburst indica or sativa?

Strawburst is best classified as a hybrid. Its genetics combine both physically relaxing and more balanced hybrid families, so the experience can begin with a brighter cerebral quality before developing stronger body relaxation.
How long does Strawburst take to flower?
Square One Genetics lists a flowering period of 60–65 days, or roughly eight-and-a-half to just over nine weeks indoors. The breeder also rates its yield as heavy.
Final Thoughts on Strawburst

Strawburst is a good example of fruit-focused breeding done with enough depth to avoid becoming one-dimensional. Strawberry Torte contributes strawberry sweetness, nuts, Purple Punch fruit, and gas, while Blueberry Fritter brings unmistakable blueberry character together with Apple Fritter’s richer pastry and funk. The resulting flower can shift from fresh berries into baked dough, nuts, earth, and fuel within the same session.

Its cultivation profile makes the cross equally interesting to growers. A 60–65 day flowering period is relatively manageable, and Square One’s heavy-yield designation gives this weed strain practical production potential in addition to its terpene appeal. Because the original release is an F1, hunting multiple seeds may reveal meaningful differences in berry balance and plant structure, giving growers room to select toward strawberry, blueberry, nuts, gas, or a combination of all four.

For cannabis enthusiasts who enjoy sweet weed but want something richer than another generic candy hybrid, Strawburst occupies an appealing middle ground. Its strongest expressions combine genuine berry character, dessert-like depth, balanced effects, and productive growth while preserving enough earth and funk to keep the flavor interesting after the first impression fades.
